correctness.rationale: In each cone write x=r m_i+z e_i with m_i the edge midpoint and z=r(u−1/2). With the calibrated coefficients the field is −a(r−1)m_i+omega_i e_i. Thus r(t) contracts exponentially toward one and z grows at speed omega_i until z=r/2; the next cone begins at z=−r/2 with the same r. Integration gives the stated switch equation. The strict speed and collar inequalities give positive angular velocity on both sides of every ray. Each trajectory stays in a radial compact subset on which the angular speed is bounded above and away from zero, so no finite-time switch accumulation occurs. Periodicity forces r=1; the cycle has edge times 1/omega_i and its return derivative follows from continuity of the return time. The coordinate identification is piecewise linear, agrees on each common ray, and intertwines forward trajectories. The cutoff is for everywhere positive angular velocity, not a maximal attraction basin. The frozen script was inspected, not run.
